notes: Section 56.11 extends §56.10's initial-disclosure restrictions to all downstream recipients. §56.10 governs the first disclosure from provider to recipient; §56.11 governs every subsequent disclosure in the chain.
Section 56.11 relies on §56.05's definition of 'medical information' and 'authorization' to determine what information is subject to the further-disclosure prohibition.
Each unauthorized further disclosure under §56.11 is independently actionable under §56.35's damages provisions.
If a recipient's failure to secure medical information leads to further unauthorized disclosure, both §56.11 (the disclosure) and §56.36 (the security failure) may apply.
HIPAA's minimum necessary standard limits downstream use and disclosure; CMIA §56.11 is stricter — it requires a NEW authorization for any further disclosure, not just a minimum-necessary limitation.
